question: My metric is a callable object with internal state, not a plain function. When DSPy asks another model to generate retry advice from that metric, what source code does it actually embed?
gold_answer: At construction time, the feedback-generating retry wrapper first tries `inspect.getsource(reward_fn)`. If that raises `TypeError`, it falls back to `inspect.getsource(reward_fn.__class__)`, which is the usual path for callable instances. On retry, that captured string is passed into the advice model as `reward_code`.

rubric.statement: `Refine.__init__` tries to capture the metric's source code by calling `inspect.getsource(reward_fn)` and storing the result in `self.reward_fn_code`.
If direct source lookup raises `TypeError`, `Refine.__init__` falls back to `inspect.getsource(reward_fn.__class__)`, so callable-object metrics contribute their class source code.
When generating retry feedback, `Refine.forward` inserts the previously captured `self.reward_fn_code` into the `reward_code` field and passes it to `dspy.Predict(OfferFeedback)`.
`OfferFeedback` defines `reward_code` as an input field representing the code of the reward function being analyzed.
